There is a close similarity between the working of Example 16.7 and an acid–base calculation. The first step (the assumption that the reaction goes to completion and is followed by a small amount of back dissociation) is analogous to the procedure for dealing with the addition of a small amount of a strong acid to a solution of a weak base. The subsequent calculation of the successive dissociation steps resembles the calculation of polyprotic acid equilibria in Example 15.15. The only difference is that in complex-ion equilibria it is conventional to work with formation constants, which are the inverse of the dissociation constants used in acid–base equilibria.
